sections.title: Regulations
text: Business Registration Ordinance (Chapter 310 of the Laws of Hong Kong)

The Business Registration Ordinance requires every person carrying on any business to make an application to the Commissioner of Inland Revenue in the prescribed manner for the registration of that business. The Commissioner of Inland Revenue must register each business for which a business registration application is made and, as soon as practicable after the prescribed business registration fee and levy are paid, issue a business registration certificate or branch registration certificate for the relevant business or the relevant branch, as the case may be.
As of the date of this prospectus, our Operating Subsidiary holds a valid business registration certificate.
Construction Workers Registration Ordinance (Chapter 583 of the Laws of Hong Kong)

The Construction Workers Registration Ordinance provides, among others, for registration and regulation of construction workers. The principal object of the Construction Workers Registration Ordinance is to establish a system for registration of construction workers and to regulate construction workers who personally carry out construction work on construction site.

Under Sections 3(1) and 5 of the Construction Workers Registration Ordinance, the principal contractors/subcontractors/employers/controllers of construction sites are required to employ only registered construction workers to personally carry out construction work on construction sites.
Factories and Industrial Undertakings Ordinance (Chapter 59 of the Laws of Hong Kong)

The Factories and Industrial Undertakings Ordinance provides for the safety and health protection of workers in an industrial undertaking. revenue.heading: Contract revenues
revenue.text:
Our contract revenues increased by 84.1% to US$15,259,555 (of which US$12,136,608 were generated from related parties) for the year ended March 31, 2026, from US$8,290,827 (of which US$5,786,743 were generated from related parties) for the year ended March 31, 2025. The contract revenues increase was principally a result of the increasing number of projects we were involved in.

The following table sets out our contract revenues generated from different services during the two years ended March 31, 2026:

Civil engineering works has become a more important source of our contract revenues during the year ended March 31, 2026, the proportion of revenue increased to 80.2%, as compared to 69.3% of total revenues during fiscal year 2025. Revenues from civil engineering works grew by 113.0% to US$12,244,657 for the

year ended March 31, 2026, from US$5,747,334 for the year ended March 31, 2025. We performed services in 19 subcontracting projects in fiscal year 2026, as compared to 13 subcontracting projects in fiscal year 2025. Our construction projects generally had a construction period of 1 to 3 years.

Soil and rock transportation services, though we recognized less revenue in fiscal 2026, remained our significant source of contract revenues. This segment contributed 13.5% and 30.7% of our contract revenues for the year ended March 31, 2026 and 2025, respectively.

tax.heading: Provision for income taxes
tax.text:
The Group is not subject to any income tax in the Cayman Islands and the BVI pursuant to the rules and regulations in those jurisdictions, but our major operating subsidiary, UPT, is subject to Hong Kong profits tax. Provision for income taxes was US$66,072 for the year ended March 31, 2026, which represented a decrease of 63.5% from US$180,942 for the year ended March 31, 2025. Effective tax rate for the years ended March 31, 2026 and 2025 was 16.5% and 14.8%, respectively.

Our net income decreased by 68.0% to US$334,429 for the year ended March 31, 2026, as compared to US$1,044,051 for the year ended March 31, 2025. Net profit margins were 2.2% and 12.6% for the year ended March 31, 2026 and 2025, respectively. The decrease in net income was mainly due to the decrease in gross profit and increase in general and administrative.

ocf.heading: Operating activities
ocf.text:
Our cash inflow from operating activities was principally receipt of payments from customers. Our cash outflows from operating activities were principally due to payments for subcontracting fees, staff costs, and administrative and other operating expenses.

Net cash provided by operating activities for the year ended March 31, 2026 was US$827,896, represented a increase of 3,649.2% as compared to fiscal year 2025 of US$22,082. The increase was mainly due to change in contract receivable, as we had slowed down the increase in contract receivable, and the increase in accounts payable.

The changes in cash flow from operating activities were attributable to the decrease of net income from US$1,044,051 for fiscal year 2025 to US$334,429 for fiscal year 2026, and the following non-cash adjustments and changes of working capital items: (i) depreciation of property and equipment of US$43,037; (ii) depreciation of property and equipment under finance lease of US$379,591; (iii) amortization of operating lease right-of-use assets and interest of lease liabilities of US$23,066; (iv) provision for allowance for expected credit losses of US$12,361; (v) increase in total contract receivable of US$1,268,804; (vi) increase of total retention receivable of US$705,716; (vii) increase of total contract assets of US$1,121,868; (viii) increase in accounts payable of US$1,019,476; (ix) increase in…

During fiscal year 2026, we recorded a loss on a third party civil engineering works project, resulting from the elevated operational risks inherent in site clearance and demolition works. Demolition works in Hong Kong carry above-average operational risks due to strict public safety requirements and the close proximity of neighboring structures. Additionally, an increasingly competitive landscape in the Hong Kong construction sector put downward pressure on project pricing, resulting in a reduction in target profit margins for us to win new work.

ga.heading: General and administrative expenses
ga.text:
For the years ended March 31, 2026 and 2025, our general and administrative expenses consisted mainly of staff cost, rental expense, legal and professional fees, accounting/audit fees, provision for expected credit loss and others.

Our general and administrative expenses increased by 26.1% to US$1,542,551 for the year ended March 31, 2026, from US$1,223,534 for the year ended March 31, 2025, principally due to the increase of expenses incurred for our IPO, legal and professional fees and provision for expected credit losses. As we had more projects on hand and increased in corporate size, we recruited more employees.

nonop.heading: Interest expenses
nonop.text: Our interest expense is mainly related to our interest expenses incurred by finance leases of motor vehicles, machinery and bank loans. Our interest expense increased by 8.0% to US$88,878 for the year ended March 31, 2026, from US$82,302 for the year ended March 31, 2025. The interest expenses increased because of new additions of motor vehicles by way of finance leases in fiscal year 2026.
